0.0.n: This is the country name, linked to コンビニ by の.

0.1.n: の connects Japan with convenience stores, identifying which country's stores are meant.

0.2.n: コンビニ is a common shortening of コンビニエンスストア; Japanese does not mark plural here.

0.3.n: は marks Japanese convenience stores as the topic of the sentence.

0.4.n: 時間 counts hours, so this expression gives the duration stores remain open.

0.5.n: いつ combines with でも here to express unrestricted timing rather than ask a question.

0.6.n: Added to いつ, でも makes いつでも, meaning at any time.

0.7.n: 開いて is the て-form of 開く; います politely describes the continuing state, not the act of opening.

1.0.n: 朝 is the first time period in a list followed by でも.

1.1.n: でも follows 朝 to include morning among the possible shopping times.

1.2.n: 夜 names another time when shopping is possible.

1.3.n: Repeating でも after 夜 adds another option to the list.

1.4.n: お昼 refers to the middle of the day here, not lunch; お makes the expression softer.

1.5.n: でも adds midday as another possible shopping time.

1.7.n: With でも, this question word becomes an expression covering all times.

1.8.n: いつでも sums up the listed times as at any time.

1.9.n: コンビニ is an everyday shortened word; no particular store is specified here.

1.10.n: で marks the place where the shopping happens.

1.11.n: This noun combines with ができます to describe an activity that is possible.

1.12.n: が marks 買い物 as the activity that is possible with できます.

1.13.n: できます is the polite form of できる, expressing that shopping is possible.

2.0.n: だから connects this situation to the previous explanation about stores being open anytime.

2.1.n: 夜 takes に here to specify when the hunger occurs.

2.2.n: に marks 夜 as the time of the event.

2.3.n: お腹 is the everyday polite word used in the expression お腹が空く for becoming hungry.

2.4.n: が marks お腹 as what becomes empty in this expression for hunger.

2.5.n: 空いた is the past form of 空く; お腹が空いた describes having become hungry.

2.6.n: 時 follows お腹が空いた to mean a time when you are hungry.

2.8.n: Here でも connects contrasting situations, unlike the でも attached to time words earlier.

2.9.n: 家 refers to the person's own home in this context.

2.10.n: に marks the location where something does not exist, rather than where an action happens.

2.11.n: 何 combines with も and the negative ない to express that nothing is available.

2.12.n: も after 何 pairs with a negative to rule out everything.

2.13.n: ない is the plain negative of ある; food is implied by the surrounding discussion of hunger.

2.14.n: 時 turns 家に何もない into a description of a particular situation.

2.15.n: は highlights this situation as the topic; the sentence continues in the next line.

3.0.n: コンビニ is the destination of the trip described here.

3.1.n: に marks the destination with 行く.

3.2.n: 行って is the irregular て-form of 行く, connecting going to the store with shopping afterward.

3.3.n: 少し describes the amount of shopping, not the number of people.

3.4.n: 買い物 combines with をする to describe the activity of buying things.

3.5.n: を marks 買い物 as the activity performed with する.

3.6.n: The plain form する ends the description placed before 人, identifying which people are meant.

3.7.n: 人 is described by everything from コンビニに through する.

3.8.n: は makes the people who go shopping the topic of the statement.

3.9.n: とても strengthens 多い, emphasizing the large number of people.

3.10.n: 多い describes the number of people; English usually expresses this as there being many people.

3.11.n: と marks the preceding statement as the content of the speaker's thought.

3.12.n: 思います is the polite form of 思う; the speaker is understood without an explicit word for I.

0.lit: As for Japan's convenience stores, they are open 24 hours, anytime.
0.tip: 開いています describes a continuing open state, not stores currently opening.

1.lit: Even morning, even night, even midday, anytime, at convenience stores shopping is possible.
1.tip: An activity noun followed by ができます expresses that you can do that activity.

2.lit: So, when at night the stomach has become empty, but when at home there is nothing, as for that,
2.tip: Here でも means but; it is not attached to a time word as in the previous line.

3.lit: As for people who go to convenience stores and do a little shopping, I think they are very numerous.
3.tip: Japanese puts the whole description before 人: people who go to the store and do a little shopping.
